notes: A new version tells you it exists. SideCut already checked for updates quietly on every launch, but unless the install sheet happened to come up you had to go to Settings → More → Check for updates to find out. The launch check now announces what it found: a notice on the boot it is discovered, and an “⬆ Update available” entry in the 🔔 bell with an Install now button that stays there (and keeps the bell badged) until you install it. It is the same check that already ran — no extra network call, no timer, nothing at all while the app is in the background

Installing from that entry is playback-safe. It goes through the same sheet as the manual check, so if a song is playing the update stages and applies when you leave the app rather than cutting the music; “Later” keeps the entry in the bell instead of hiding the news

Plays are counted honestly now. A play was written the moment playback started, so tapping through a list for two seconds each inflated songs played, most played and top artists. A play now counts only once you pass the HALFWAY POINT of a track, or it plays through to its natural end. Recently played is untouched — that stays based on when you started the song. Both the stats page and the stats bubble say so

The tutorial teaches with scenarios. A new “Common scenarios, step by step” section walks through six real jobs: getting one song off Spotify into SideCut for free, building your own album out of songs from different playlists, reordering an album’s songs without misfiring (the 3-second hold), jumping back to the song that is playing, backing up or moving to a new phone, and keeping SideCut updated without digging for it. It also states the new play-counting rule

The tutorial summary in Settings → More carries the same scenarios in short, so the text version matches the walkthrough — including the albums-are-yours note. And “Read the whole thing” on the What’s new popup now closes the popup and opens the 🔔 bell with the complete patch notes, instead of unrolling a cramped scroll box that duplicated them
